activities.name: Gies is very competitive. Writing the essay for a second major you didn’t apply
activities.description: Gies is very competitive. Writing the essay for a second major you didn’t apply to almost certainly hurt you. Imagine an Econ dean reading your essay that’s all about political science. It’s not going to create a great impression. Your GPA is decent, but likely far below the average Gies admit. I’m not sure what you mean by a feeder school. I think any high school in Illinois is a feeder to UIUC and I can’t imagine one benefits you over another.

activities.name: - Hi. I am sorry about the rejection. Re, GPA - UIUC doesn’t do weighted GPA. Th
activities.description: - Hi. I am sorry about the rejection. Re, GPA - UIUC doesn’t do weighted GPA. They only do UW. For Gies, their lower end of UW is 3.8, so unfortunately 3.6 is lower than what they are looking for.

activities.name: Test optional doesn’t help either. It could have been ok if your GPA was amazing
activities.description: Test optional doesn’t help either. It could have been ok if your GPA was amazing and ECs and essays are great… but lower than average GPA & so-so ECs will not offset test optional. Not sure about LAS but maybe that hiccup with the essay factored in.

activities.name: And from what I have seen, a feeder school isn’t always a good thing - they can’
activities.description: And from what I have seen, a feeder school isn’t always a good thing - they can’t accept 100 graduates from the same school, so in your case you may have had better odds if you were from some tiny HS in some rural location in Southern IL compared to Walter Payton.
